title: Trump Claims 2022 Midterm Losses Were Stolen — No Evidence
description_short: Trump Claims 2022 Midterm Losses Were Stolen — No Evidence
description_medium: After Republican candidates underperformed in the November 2022 midterms, Donald Trump claimed that some results were stolen, focusing particularly on Arizona’s governor’s race. Democrat Katie Hobbs defeated Trump-backed Kari Lake. The supplied account says election officials, investigations and courts rejected fraud claims, but the linked Investing.com page returned HTTP 403 and specific statements or proceedings are not included.
description_long: Following the 2022 midterm elections, Donald Trump challenged results in races where candidates he supported lost. The supplied account focuses on Arizona, where Democrat Katie Hobbs defeated Kari Lake, whom Trump had backed. It says Trump claimed the race was stolen despite audits and investigations finding no evidence of fraud, and that election officials and courts rejected the claims. title: Trump Shuffles Slowly Down West Point Ramp, Sparking Health Speculation
description_short: Trump Shuffles Slowly Down West Point Ramp, Sparking Health Speculation
description_medium: After delivering the June 13, 2020, West Point commencement address, Donald Trump was filmed walking slowly down a ramp with military officers beside him. He later said the ramp was slippery and that he ran the final 10 feet. The video documents his gait and public explanation but does not establish a medical condition.

title: Trump Lifts Russia Sanctions on Oleg Deripaska's Aluminum Company
description_short: Trump Lifts Russia Sanctions on Oleg Deripaska's Aluminum Company
description_medium: On January 27, 2019, the Treasury Department lifted sanctions on En+, Rusal and EuroSibEnergo after the companies reduced Oleg Deripaska’s direct and indirect ownership stakes and severed his control. Treasury said independent directors would hold a majority on the En+ and Rusal boards. Deripaska himself remained on the sanctions list; the official release describes the companies’ delisting, not his.
description_long: On January 27, 2019, the Trump Treasury Department formally lifted sanctions on three companies controlled by Russian oligarch Oleg Deripaska — including aluminum giant Rusal, the world's second-largest aluminum producer — over the objections of Senate Democrats who had tried to block the move. Deripaska is a close associate of Vladimir Putin and was himself under sanctions. The deal required Deripaska to reduce his personal ownership stakes in the companies but did not sanction him individually. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called the move a 'gift to Putin' and noted that Paul Manafort — who had worked for Deripaska — had owed him tens of millions of dollars. The Treasury Department's justification that Deripaska had ceded 'control' was disputed by critics who noted his continued influence over the companies through family members and associates. The decision was one of several instances in which Trump moved to benefit Russian oligarchs connected to Kremlin power.
notes: The Treasury release confirms the delisting of three companies after ownership and governance changes and states that Deripaska's personal sanctions remained. The populated long also includes claims about political influence and continued control that the release does not substantiate; its correction is outside the fields assigned here.

title: Musk DOGE Accesses Treasury Payment Systems Without Authorization
description_short: Musk DOGE Accesses Treasury Payment Systems Without Authorization
description_medium: Elon Musk's DOGE operatives accessed the Treasury Department's Bureau of the Fiscal Service payment systems without legal authorization, gaining read and potential write access to the infrastructure that distributes trillions of dollars in federal payments, Social Security benefits, Medicare reimbursements, and federal employee salaries. A career Treasury official resigned rather than grant the access and warned of catastrophic fraud and national security risks. Federal courts issued orders blocking the access but enforcement remained uncertain as the administration claimed presidential authority.
description_long: The linked Reuters report describes a February 2025 preliminary injunction blocking Department of Government Efficiency personnel from accessing Treasury systems while a lawsuit by 19 states proceeded. U.S. District Judge Jeannette Vargas said the states were likely correct that DOGE lacked legal authority for access and found that Treasury had not adequately considered the risk of exposing sensitive state banking information. The ruling addressed a temporary legal restriction and the risks alleged by the states. It does not establish from Treasury system logs whether DOGE personnel had previously logged in, what permissions any individual held, or whether they viewed, changed or exported data. The populated medium states that DOGE operatives accessed the systems and had read and potential write access, but the linked article does not supply Treasury records to verify those details. It also does not itself establish that access was unlawful as a final merits finding. Access logs, permission records, Treasury approvals and final court findings are needed to resolve what access occurred and under what authority.
notes: The supplied Reuters account supports a preliminary injunction sought by 19 states and a judge's view that the states were likely to prevail on authority and disclosure-risk arguments. It does not establish actual system access, individual permissions, data use, or a final ruling. Those records remain necessary to complete the access claim.

title: Disbands NSC Pandemic Response Unit
description_short: The White House eliminated the National Security Council’s global health security team, weakening pandemic preparedness.
description_medium: The NSC's global health security unit monitored emerging outbreaks, coordinated agencies and supported science-based White House communication. A contemporaneous Los Angeles Times account attributed its disbandment to national security adviser John Bolton and quoted the administration describing a streamlining effort. The full staff roster, reassignment of duties and operational effects are not documented in that report.
description_long: The White House’s National Security Council had a global health security and biodefense unit responsible for watching for emerging outbreaks, coordinating federal agencies, and supporting public communication grounded in science.
